prerequisites: Having passed the Fluid Mechanics course.
Knowledge of the fundamental equations governing fluid motion.
Concepts of boundary layer, potential flow, and energy equation.
Viscous flow in ducts and turbulence.

learning_outcomes.text: Basic concepts of the types of fluid dynamic systems and their application.
Principles of energy transfer in fluid transport systems and power systems.
Typology, design, and fundamental characteristics of fluid machines.
Knowledge of the application of similarity techniques in turbomachines.
Identification of phenomena limiting machine operation.
Relationship between the energy managed by machines and the energy levels of the circuits in which they operate.
Knowledge of oleohydraulic and pneumatic technologies.
Methodologies for analysis and experimentation in Fluid Engineering.
Understand and apply the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Perform measurements of fluid-mechanical variables and performance tests of fluid machines.
Design, calculate, project, and operate fluid transport systems.
Model, analyze, and optimize the operation of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards related to fluid machines and systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fluid machines and systems
General principles of energy transfer in turbomachines
Generating machines: pumps, fans, and compressors
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as 0.7 times the Final Exam (EF) score plus 0.3 times the Other Elements (OE) score. A minimum score of 4.0 out of 10 is required on the Final Exam (EF) to pass the course. If the EF score is less than 4.0, the final grade (NF) will be the minimum of 4.0 or the calculated NF. In extraordinary evaluations, if a student has not attended classes and thus has OE = 0, the written exam will be the only assessment, weighted at 70%, meaning the maximum possible grade in these evaluations would be 70%.
